summary: At every start the v0.12.26 engine emits exactly 24 `capability_activation` frames announcing the activation lifecycle of 8 internal capabilities. Six reach `ready`; three stop at `stage:"unavailable", reason:"disabled_by_config"` (pricing_refresher, learned_policy, smart_handoff) and one at `reason:"isolation_not_enforced"` (delegate_isolation). Darhai currently drops all 24 silently via ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS. The work is: decode them in the already-built-but-empty capability dispatcher, keep an engine-readiness record, and turn on the one gate I could actually identify by measurement — `[compact] smart_enabled = true`, which flips smart_handoff from `disabled_by_config` to `ready` (measured, isolated home, single-variable run).
userValue: Two concrete gains. (1) Smart compaction is currently OFF for every Darhai user: `smart_handoff` reports `disabled_by_config` and I measured that `[compact] smart_enabled = true` alone turns it on (trigger/release fractions, cooldown, min-shrink, and with `smart_handoff_to_memory` a handoff of compacted context into long-term memory). Darhai users run into compaction constantly — task #96 in this repo is literally "context ran to 1.4M". Enabling it is a real behavioural improvement, not telemetry. (2) `delegate_isolation: isolation_not_enforced` is a safety fact the user cannot currently see, and Darhai advertises sub-agents (`sub_agent_traces: true` in the measured ready caps, and a `sub_agent_event` decoder arm). The engine is saying delegate isolation is not being enforced on this platform; today that statement is thrown away. Beyond those two, the event itself makes "why is smart compaction not doing anything" answerable instead of invisible.

protocolTypes.name: EngineCapabilityId
protocolTypes.tsDefinition:
/**
 * Engine capability ids carried by `capability_activation`.
 *
 * MEASURED on wayland-core 0.12.26 (isolated WAYLAND_HOME, `--json-stream`,
 * empty stdin): these 8 appear at every start, in this emission order. The
 * same 8 names are interned as one contiguous run in the binary's serde table,
 * so this is the complete v0.12.26 set — but the contract does not declare it,
 * so treat it as open (see the widened union member below).
 */
export type EngineCapabilityId =
  | 'pricing_refresher'
  | 'mid_flight_monitor'
  | 'cooldown_tracker'
  | 'learned_policy'
  | 'smart_handoff'
  | 'delegate_isolation'
  | 'procedure_skill_drafting'
  | 'legacy_auto_skill_drafting';
protocolTypes.contractPath: tests/fixtures/engine-contract/desktop/v1/schema/producer-complete.schema.json (anyOf[76], "Non-Desktop producer inventory discriminator" — declares ONLY `type`; the ids below are measured from the binary, not from the contract)

protocolTypes.name: CapabilityActivationStage
protocolTypes.tsDefinition:
/**
 * Activation lifecycle stage.
 *
 * MEASURED on the wire: 'declared' | 'configured' | 'constructed' | 'ready' |
 * 'unavailable'. Two further members ('reached', 'outcome_changed') are
 * interned adjacent to 'declared'/'constructed'/'unavailable' in the binary's
 * variant table and correspond to the TUI's "runtime path reached" /
 * "outcome changed" labels, so they are included; I did NOT observe them on
 * the wire in any run.
 */
export type CapabilityActivationStage =
  | 'declared'
  | 'configured'
  | 'constructed'
  | 'reached'
  | 'ready'
  | 'outcome_changed'
  | 'unavailable';
protocolTypes.contractPath: tests/fixtures/engine-contract/desktop/v1/schema/producer-complete.schema.json (anyOf[76] — no payload properties at all; stage values are measured)

protocolTypes.name: CapabilityUnavailableReason
protocolTypes.tsDefinition:
/**
 * Why a capability stopped at `stage: 'unavailable'`.
 *
 * The five wire values are one contiguous interned run in the binary,
 * immediately after the `capability` / `stage` field names. The engine's TUI
 * renders them as: "disabled by configuration", "required dependency
 * unavailable", "no production constructor", "runtime path not wired",
 * "isolation not enforced". That TUI list carries a SIXTH phrase, "invalid
 * activation evidence", for which I found no matching wire token — hence the
 * widened member below.
 *
 * MEASURED at v0.12.26 defaults: pricing_refresher / learned_policy /
 * smart_handoff -> 'disabled_by_config'; delegate_isolation ->
 * 'isolation_not_enforced'.
 */
export type CapabilityUnavailableReason =
  | 'disabled_by_config'
  | 'dependency_unavailable'
  | 'no_production_constructor'
  | 'runtime_path_unwired'
  | 'isolation_not_enforced';
protocolTypes.contractPath: tests/fixtures/engine-contract/desktop/v1/schema/producer-complete.schema.json (anyOf[76]); reason tokens measured from the binary string table

protocolTypes.name: WCoreCapabilityActivationEvent
protocolTypes.contractPath: tests/fixtures/engine-contract/desktop/v1/schema/producer-complete.schema.json (anyOf[76]) — the contract marks ONLY `type` as required and sets additionalProperties:true, so `capability` and `stage` are NOT contract-required; they were present on 24/24 measured frames. Declare them required in TS and validate at the handler boundary (the handler receives Record<string, unknown> anyway), do not trust them blindly. Do NOT add this member to the `WCoreEvent` union — see handlerWork; export it as a standalone `WCoreCapabilityActivationEvent` type alias instead, or two green tests turn red.

handlerWork.change: Add the four types above as standalone exports near the bottom, AFTER the `WCoreEvent` union closes (it ends at line 279 with the `cua_policy_denied` member) and BEFORE the `ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS` block at line 335. Export `WCoreCapabilityActivationEvent` as a plain type alias (strip the leading `|`), NOT as a member of `WCoreEvent`. Then DELETE line 349 — `'capability_activation', // observed only; not in the contract bundle` — from ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS, and update the JSDoc at lines 322-323 which currently says "a single engine start emits 27 of them (`capability_activation` alone 24 times)" — after this change the acknowledged list covers 3 lines per start, not 27.
handlerWork.why: Two existing tests make this exact placement load-bearing. `tests/unit/wcore-eventCoverage.test.ts:57-61` fails if a name is in BOTH the WCoreEvent union and ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS (its `handledEventTypes()` regexes `type:\s*'([a-z_]+)'` over the union block only, so a standalone alias is invisible to it). `tests/unit/wcore-capabilityDispatch.test.ts:201-202` fails if a type claimed by a registered capability is ALSO in the acknowledged list. Claiming the event in the dispatcher therefore REQUIRES removing it from the acknowledged list, and adding it to WCoreEvent as well would be a third, unnecessary way to break the pair.

handlerWork.change: NEW file. Export `const capabilityActivationCapability: CapabilityHandler = { name: 'capability_activation', handles: ['capability_activation'], handle(event, ctx) { ... } }` against the contract in `capabilities/types.ts` (lines 60-76). `handle` must: (a) runtime-narrow `event.capability` and `event.stage` to non-empty strings and `return false` if either is missing — falling through is the honest answer and the dispatcher treats false as unhandled; (b) accumulate into a module-local `Map<string, {stage, reason}>` keyed by capability, last-write-wins, so the 24 frames collapse to an 8-row readiness record; (c) `ctx.log` at 'declared'/'configured'/'constructed'/'ready' (quiet — 20 of the 24 frames are these); (d) `ctx.warn` ONCE per capability when `stage === 'unavailable'`, including `capability` and `reason`, because that is the operator-visible contract violation case the context doc at types.ts:57 reserves warn for; (e) `ctx.emit({ type: 'capability_activation', data: { capability, stage, reason }, msg_id: ctx.activeMsgId() })` so WCoreManager can forward it; (f) `return true`. Keep it synchronous — types.ts:30-31 makes that an invariant. Export a `readCapabilityActivationSnapshot()` accessor over the Map for diagnostics and tests. Reset the Map when a new `ready` is seen — NOTE: the handler never sees `ready` (it is a real WCoreEvent arm at index.ts:519), so export a `resetCapabilityActivation()` and call it from that arm, otherwise a restarted engine leaves stale rows.
handlerWork.why: `src/process/agent/wcore/capabilities/index.ts:27` declares `const HANDLERS: readonly CapabilityHandler[] = []` — the registry is built, documented (types.ts:7-32 names "capability activation" as one of the nine intended modules) and empty. This is the designed landing spot: the dispatcher already contains throws (index.ts:86-92) and already runs before the acknowledged-unhandled check at index.ts:969-971 of the agent, so nothing in the 1146-line decoder needs touching.

handlerWork.change: Import `capabilityActivationCapability` and add it as the single element of the `HANDLERS` array at line 27.
handlerWork.why: `assertNoOverlap` runs at module load via `createDispatcher(HANDLERS)` on line 96, so registration is checked at startup and in every test that imports the module.

handlerWork.change: In the existing `case 'ready':` arm (lines 519-524), call `resetCapabilityActivation()` alongside `this.capabilities = event.capabilities`. No other change to this file — the `default:` arm at line 962 already routes through `dispatchCapabilityEvent` at line 969.
handlerWork.why: Per-start state must not survive a respawn. WCoreAgent restarts the child process (spawn at line 317); without a reset the readiness record would show the previous process's outcomes.

handlerWork.change: Add `export type WcoreCompactSection = { smart_enabled?: boolean; smart_handoff_to_memory?: boolean; smart_trigger_fraction?: number; smart_release_fraction?: number; smart_cooldown_turns?: number; smart_min_shrink_tokens?: number; [key: string]: unknown }` next to the other section types (lines 34-48), plus `getCompactSection(path?)` / `setCompactSection(value, path?)` following the exact shape of `getMemorySection`/`setMemorySection` at lines 189-196. These key names are measured from the engine's `[compact]` serde field run in the binary; `smart_enabled` is the one I proved flips the capability.
handlerWork.why: This is the gate. `[compact] smart_enabled = true` alone moved smart_handoff from `unavailable/disabled_by_config` to `declared -> configured -> constructed -> ready` in an otherwise-empty isolated home. The bridge's lossless read-modify-write (documented lines 22-26) means adding `[compact]` cannot clobber the rest of a user's config.

handlerWork.change: NOTHING. Verify only. `ipcBridge.wcoreConfig.getSection` / `setSection` (lines 79 and 89) are already generic over the section name, and `src/common/adapter/bridgeAllowlist.ts:233-239` already remote-denies all three `wcoreConfig.*` verbs.
handlerWork.why: `[compact]` mutation reaches the renderer through the existing human-only, remote-denied path with zero new IPC surface. Adding a bespoke verb here would create a second, unaudited door into the same file.

uiWork.change: Add a 'Smart compaction' switch bound to the engine `[compact]` section — copy the exact pattern this file already uses: `getSection<MemorySection>('memory')` at line 34 and `setSection('memory', next)` at line 45, but against `'compact'` and `smart_enabled`. Add a second, dependent switch for `smart_handoff_to_memory` (disabled while `smart_enabled` is false — MEASURED: `smart_handoff_to_memory` alone does nothing, `smart_enabled` alone is sufficient). MemoryPane is the right home rather than RuntimePane because the handoff target is long-term memory. New i18n keys in mn-MN and en-US; run `bun run i18n:types && node scripts/check-i18n.js` per AGENTS.md.

Add a small engine-capability readout: 8 rows of `capability -> stage`, with `unavailable` rows showing the reason. It must surface `delegate_isolation: isolation_not_enforced` in particular, because Darhai exposes sub-agents and this is the engine stating that delegate isolation is NOT being enforced. Data comes from `readCapabilityActivationSnapshot()` in the main process; it needs a read-only IPC verb, and that verb MUST be added to `src/common/adapter/bridgeAllowlist.ts` next to the `wcoreConfig.getSection` deny at line 235 — it discloses engine security posture, the same rationale the comment there already gives. If the effort budget is tight, ship this second and the MemoryPane toggle first; the toggle is the part with user-visible behaviour.

testWork.what: NEW. Drive the handler through `createDispatcher([capabilityActivationCapability])` — the same function production calls, per the convention stated at the top of wcore-capabilityDispatch.test.ts. Prove: (1) all 24 measured frames replay to an 8-row snapshot with the measured terminal stages (6 x ready, pricing_refresher/learned_policy/smart_handoff = unavailable+disabled_by_config, delegate_isolation = unavailable+isolation_not_enforced); (2) exactly 4 warns are emitted, one per unavailable capability, and re-delivering the same unavailable frame does not warn twice; (3) a frame missing `capability` or missing `stage` returns false (contract marks only `type` required, so this is the real wire risk, not a hypothetical); (4) `reason` present on a non-'unavailable' stage is tolerated and recorded, since additionalProperties:true means the engine may add fields; (5) `resetCapabilityActivation()` clears the snapshot. MUTATION CHECK: temporarily make `handle` always return true for a frame with no `capability` and confirm test (3) goes red — a snapshot test that cannot fail is worth nothing.
fixtures: NEW tests/fixtures/engine-contract/desktop/v1/observed/capability_activation.jsonl — the 24 lines are not in the contract bundle and must be captured from the binary. Reproduce exactly: mkdir an isolated dir, then `WAYLAND_HOME=<dir> ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-dummy resources/bundled-wayland-core/win32-x64/wayland-core.exe --json-stream < /dev/null` and keep the lines where type == capability_activation. The dummy key is required — without any key the engine exits at init with `init_failed` before emitting any capability frame. Verbatim content measured on 0.12.26: pricing_refresher declared|unavailable(disabled_by_config); mid_flight_monitor declared|configured|constructed|ready; cooldown_tracker declared|configured|constructed|ready; learned_policy declared|unavailable(disabled_by_config); smart_handoff declared|unavailable(disabled_by_config); delegate_isolation declared|unavailable(isolation_not_enforced); procedure_skill_drafting declared|configured|constructed|ready; legacy_auto_skill_drafting declared|configured|constructed|ready.

tests/fixtures/engine-contract/desktop/v1/adversarial/events/unknown-noncritical.jsonl — {"critical":false,"payload":{},"type":"future_observation"}. Proves the dispatcher declines a type nobody claims and the event still falls through to the acknowledged-unhandled check. Relevant here because capability_activation frames carry NO `critical` field at all (measured), i.e. they are non-critical by omission.

tests/fixtures/engine-contract/desktop/v1/adversarial/events/unknown-critical.jsonl — {"critical":true,"type":"future_authority"}. Proves claiming capability_activation did not accidentally widen the dispatcher into swallowing unknown-critical events, which must still reach the reject path.

testWork.what: MUST be edited or it goes red. The case at lines ~76-80 ('covers the variants a v0.12.26 engine start actually emits') asserts ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS.has('capability_activation'). Do not just delete the name from the array — replace the assertion with the honest invariant: each of ['execution_policy','workspace_policy','capability_activation','provider_attempt'] must be EITHER in ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS OR in claimedEventTypes() from '@process/agent/wcore/capabilities'. That version keeps proving 'this never warns on every engine start' and does not need editing again when the next capability lands. Also re-check the cap at line ~73 (`size <= 30`).

No edit needed, but it becomes the regression guard: the case at lines 201-202 (claimed types must not also be listed inert) now has a real handler to check, and 'the production dispatcher is callable and declines what nobody claims' at line 205 now runs against a non-empty HANDLERS. Confirm both still pass.

Extend the existing suite: setCompactSection({ smart_enabled: true }) on a config that already has [tools], [security], [mcp.servers.*] must leave every other section byte-identical (the lossless invariant at configBridge.ts:22-26), and must round-trip through getCompactSection. Add a negative: setCompactSection must not be reachable from a remote caller — assert 'wcoreConfig.setSection' is present in the remote-deny list in src/common/adapter/bridgeAllowlist.ts.

testWork.testFile: scripts/measure-capability-activation.mjs (new, invoked manually; mirror of the existing scripts/measure-approval-order.mjs referenced at protocol.ts:333)
testWork.what: Re-derivation harness for the next engine bump: boot the bundled binary in a throwaway WAYLAND_HOME twice — once with no config and once with `[compact] smart_enabled = true` — and print the capability/stage/reason table for each. The second run MUST show smart_handoff reaching ready; if it does not, the gate moved and MemoryPane's toggle is lying to the user. This is the counter-check, not the happy path: it is the only thing that catches an engine bump silently renaming the key.

risks: THE CONTRACT TELLS YOU ALMOST NOTHING ABOUT THIS EVENT. `capability_activation` is absent from manifest.json, absent from events/, and absent from core-event.schema.json. Its only appearance is producer-complete.schema.json anyOf[76], a bare `type` enum with additionalProperties:true and zero payload properties. DEFERRED.md states this outright: 'A host can therefore recognise the tag and can validate NOTHING about the body.' Every field name, stage value and reason value in this plan comes from running the binary and from its interned string tables — not from the contract. Treat `capability`/`stage` as untrusted at the decode boundary.

THE CONTRACT AND THE GAP-MATRIX DISAGREE, AND I TRUSTED THE CONTRACT. gap-matrix.json contains no mention of `capability_activation`, `workspace_policy`, `pricing_refresher` or `smart_handoff` at all — it only knows `execution_policy`. The gap matrix is silent, not wrong, but it cannot be used to scope this capability; DEFERRED.md's 'Producer events with NO Desktop payload schema' list is the authoritative statement of the hole.

I COULD NOT IDENTIFY THE GATES FOR pricing_refresher OR learned_policy. Both report `disabled_by_config`, so a config key exists, but I did not find it. MEASURED AND RULED OUT (each re-run in a fresh isolated home, capability stayed `unavailable/disabled_by_config`): `[provider_policy] require_fresh_pricing = true`; `[provider_policy] require_priced = true`; `[memory] enabled = true`; `[security] enabled = true`; all five `[observability]` flags true; `[crucible] enabled = true`; `[anvil] enabled = true`; `[compact] smart_handoff_to_memory = true`; and env vars WAYLAND_PRICING_AUTO_REFRESH=1, =true, plus WAYLAND_CONTRADICTION / WAYLAND_STALENESS / WAYLAND_KG / WAYLAND_H3 / WAYLAND_MEMORY / WAYLAND_AUTO_MEMORIZE / WAYLAND_MODEL_DISCOVERY / WAYLAND_CACHE_LEDGER. The eight capability names appear in the binary ONLY inside the protocol event-name table, never near any config key, so the gate names differ from the capability names and cannot be read off the strings. Settling this needs either upstream source (FerroxLabs/wayland-core) or the engine's own TUI, which has a CAPABILITIES panel that renders 'set <X> to enable' / 'env <VAR>' hints — I could not drive a TUI from this environment. Do NOT ship a settings toggle for either of these on a guess.

delegate_isolation IS PROBABLY NOT A CONFIG TOGGLE AT ALL. Its reason is `isolation_not_enforced`, a distinct token from `disabled_by_config` — the engine is reporting a runtime/platform fact, not an opt-out. It stayed unavailable even with the workspace sandbox active (the same run's `workspace_policy` reported profile=strict, backend=appcontainer on Windows). Whether it can ever reach ready on win32, or only under bubblewrap on Linux, can only be settled by running the binary on another platform. Report it, do not offer to 'fix' it.

THE STAGE ENUM MAY BE WIDER THAN WHAT I SAW. Five values appear on the wire (declared/configured/constructed/ready/unavailable). Two more (`reached`, `outcome_changed`) sit in the binary's variant table next to them and match TUI labels, but I never observed them — likely they only fire on capabilities that produce a verified runtime outcome during a real turn, which my empty-stdin boots never reached. Likewise the TUI has a sixth failure phrase, 'invalid activation evidence', with no wire token I could find. Hence the `| (string & {})` widening; do not narrow it to a closed union.

THE 24 COUNT IS NOT A CONTRACT. It is 8 capabilities x their path length at the current default config. Turning `[compact] smart_enabled` on changes it to 26 (smart_handoff gains configured/constructed/ready and loses one unavailable). Any test asserting a literal 24 will break the moment the toggle ships — assert per-capability terminal state instead.

SHARED-FILE COLLISION WITH THE OTHER CAPABILITY AGENTS. `capabilities/index.ts` line 27 (`HANDLERS = []`) and the ACKNOWLEDGED_UNHANDLED_EVENTS block in protocol.ts are the two files every one of the nine capability implementations must touch. Expect a conflict on both; the import list and the acknowledged-list deletions merge cleanly if each agent adds/removes only its own line.

ADJACENT, UNVERIFIED, NOT MINE TO FIX: `src/renderer/pages/settings/WCoreConfig/panes/RuntimePane.tsx:33,49` reads and writes a `[runtime]` section of the engine config.toml. `runtime` does not appear in the top-level Config field run I extracted from the binary (default, security, execution, providers, profiles, tools, session, inbound_webhook, compact, plan, file_cache, hooks, mcp, debug, observability, provider_chain, provider_policy, budget, storage, memory, browser, session_cap, crucible, anvil). My extraction may be incomplete because serde field runs are deduplicated, so this is a lead, not a finding — but do NOT copy RuntimePane's section name as the model for the `[compact]` pane without checking it.

Reading `%APPDATA%/wayland-core/config.toml` to establish the live baseline exposed a plaintext third-party API key at `[mcp.servers.wayland-image-generation.env]`. That is a pre-existing condition of this machine's config, unrelated to this capability, and I did not modify or copy it — but any diagnostics readout that ever renders engine config sections must go through the existing `sanitizeSecuritySection` path in wcoreConfigBridge.ts:48, not raw.
